title: Unemployment Insurance Appeals: Docketing a Filed Appeal and Setting Its First Hearing (System Reference)
content:
**Unemployment Insurance Appeals — docketing and the first hearing setting.** When the appeals office dockets an appeal filed on a docket that holds hearings, it sets the first hearing by telephone, mails the hearing notice today and notifies every interested party of the docket. The first hearing is set on the first hearing date that the first-setting rules give, the hearing notice is mailed at least the notice minimum days before the hearing date, and every interested party of the docket is notified.

## Where it applies

An appeal standing at filed status on a docket that holds hearings is due to be docketed and set for its first hearing. Docketing moves the appeal from filed to scheduled status: the appeal is docketed and its first hearing is set. The result governed here is the first hearing date, expressed as the first-setting notice period — the whole number of calendar days from today, the day the notice is mailed, to the first hearing date.

## Effect on the record

One docketing does all of the following on the appeal:

- the appeal moves from filed to **scheduled** status;
- the first hearing date is recorded on the appeal as its hearing date;
- the first hearing setting is entered on the appeal's activity as a hearing-setting record: a telephone hearing at 09:00 local time on the hearing date, notice mailed today, marked as the first (initial) setting;
- every interested party sees the new hearing date on the appeal and in the activity history.

## The tool: `docket_appeal_hearing_a28520da`

**How it is invoked.** An agent-side tool: the agent unlocks `docket_appeal_hearing_a28520da` and then calls it.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `appeal_id` | the docket number of the filed appeal to be set for hearing, read from the appeal lookup (`find_appeals`) before the call | identifier text |
| `notice_period_days` | the whole number of calendar days from today's date — the notice mailing date, counted as day 0 — to the first hearing date | an integer of at least 1; the tool records the hearing date as the YYYY-MM-DD date that many calendar days after today |

**Return.** A text receipt of a dictionary with: `appeal_id` (the docket number), `appeal_event_id` (the reference number of the hearing-setting record), `status` (always "scheduled" after a successful call), `hearing_date` (YYYY-MM-DD), `hearing_time` ("09:00"), `hearing_mode` ("telephone") and `notice_mailed_date` (today's date, YYYY-MM-DD). The call has succeeded when the receipt shows status scheduled and the hearing date.

*Input and receipt (hypothetical):* called on 15 April 2026 with `notice_period_days` 19, the receipt shows `status` "scheduled", `hearing_date` "2026-05-04", `hearing_time` "09:00", `hearing_mode` "telephone" and `notice_mailed_date` "2026-04-15".

## Questions answered

- *Does a docketed appeal keep filed status?* No. After docketing it stands at scheduled status with its first hearing setting on its activity.
- *In what mode is the first hearing set?* By telephone, at 09:00 local time.
